original_idea.body:
# Causal Chain: From Open-Weight Release to Criminal Capability Acquisition — Time-to-Weaponization Analysis

**Problem:** When a capable open-weight model is released, how quickly can criminal actors fine-tune or configure it to remove safety behaviors and deploy it for dual-use cyber tasks? This time-to-weaponization metric is ungoverned.

**Direction:** Analyze publicly documented cases of fine-tuning or uncensoring of open-weight models (Wizard-Vicuna, Dolphin, etc.). Estimate the time and skill required to: (a) remove refusal behaviors, (b) achieve parity with frontier model cyber capability, (c) deploy in an operational context. Assess implications for open-weight release governance.

**Why it matters:** If time-to-weaponization is measured in days and requires only modest skill, open-weight model release governance must be much more restrictive than current norms to prevent harm.

**Relevant context:** Bengio et al. open-weight challenges; NIST AI 800-1 open model appendix; Llama 3.1 70B capabilities.
